Definition: from G3326; middle (as an adjective or (neuter) noun):--among, X before them, between, + forth, mid(-day, -night), midst, way.
BiblicalUsage: Mesos is the middle, the midst, among, between, and it is the word for where Jesus stands. Matthew 18:20 promises that where two or three are gathered in His name, there am I in the midst of them, and Luke 24:36 has Jesus Himself stand in the midst of them and say, Peace be unto you. John 1:26 has John say there standeth one among you, whom ye know not, and 2 Thessalonians 2:7 says the restrainer will be taken out of the way.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the middle is where Jesus puts Himself: among the gathered, among the frightened, among those who do not know Him yet. My position is that the church is not built around an empty centre but around a present Lord.
RelatedEvents: Jesus Appears to the Disciples on Easter Evening
